extracted_claims.text: Article 43 provides two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics), the provider may choose internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII), depending on whether harmonised standards/common specifications have been applied.

Annex VII (third-party notified body assessment) is mandatory for certain systems such as biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure AI, while most other high-risk AI systems can use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.

Providers may choose any notified body for the conformity assessment procedure under Annex VII, except that where a high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems designed to continue learning after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority to derogate from the Article 43 conformity assessment procedure and authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited time, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life/health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

Under Annex VII, where necessary and after other means have been exhausted, a notified body may, upon reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 43(5) gives the Commission power to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII procedures in light of technical progress.
Notified bodies issue certification decisions as part of the Annex VII assessment of quality management systems and technical documentation.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.

A Council document references Article 30 of a related Regulation establishing AI conformity assessment body (AIP) codes and categories corresponding to Annex I AI systems, to be used in the NANDO database.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes amendments creating a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories of AI systems for the NANDO notified-body information system, and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act is still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device AI systems.
Post-2026, notified bodies designated under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, intersecting with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments.

As of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (under the Medical Devices Regulation and In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation), separate from AI Act designations.
The Commission publishes a list of designated notified bodies in the NANDO information system, filterable by legislation.

Under the Cyber Resilience Act (a separate but related regulation), as of late June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity and full application from 11 December 2027.

August 2026 is cited as the deadline by which high-risk AI obligations under the AI Act fully apply, and by which SaaS providers must issue EU Declarations of Conformity referencing the Article 43 procedure followed (Annex VI or VII) and notified body information where applicable.

A news blog reports that under a 'final text agreed in September 2026,' the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III have been moved to apply from 2 August 2029, rather than the previously reported 2 December 2027, due to unreadiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.

report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems under Article 43: internal control (Annex VI) or third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) (low confidence). While the legal framework is reasonably well-documented, the practical infrastructure of designated notified bodies remains underdeveloped, with reports as of early-to-mid 2026 indicating limited or no formal AI Act-specific designations in several sectors (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 provides two pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For biometric systems listed in point 1 of Annex III, providers may choose internal control or notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Some industry sources interpret Annex VII as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment, though this interpretation carries low confidence ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation (Section A of Annex I, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Notified Body Selection and Procedural Rules
Providers may choose any notified body under Annex VII, except where high-risk AI systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 procedures temporarily for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, as a last resort, request access to training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Administrative Infrastructure
Article 35 establishes rules for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A Council document references proposed Article 30 codes for AI conformity assessment bodies to be used in the NANDO database (medium confidence), and a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing such codes while amending aviation regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf), [COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are separate from AI Act designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Industry sources report that as of March–April 2026, the AI Act notified body ecosystem remains under construction, with no formal AI Act designations yet for medical device AI systems (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A comparable pattern is reported under the separate Cyber Resilience Act, where zero notified bodies had been designated as of late June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on the applicable deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations: most cite 2 August 2026, while one low-reliability, undated news blog claims a "final text agreed in September 2026" pushed this to 2 August 2029 via an intermediate 2 December 2027 date — this claim is uncorroborated by any official source and should be treated with strong skepticism (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026) vs. [unverified blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). Several claims regarding delegated acts under Article 43(5), notified-body certification mechanics, and Article 35 administrative rules rest on single low-authority sources (confidence 0.03–0.17) and should not be treated as settled.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2026 Annex III deadline has actually been amended, and if so, by what formal instrument. The precise, verified count of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act (versus MDR/IVDR/CRA) is unavailable. The exact boundary between Annex VI and Annex VII applicability beyond biometrics is not fully specified. The adoption status of COM(2025) 836 and the Article 30 AIP codes is unresolved, as is whether Article 43(5) delegated acts updating Annexes VI/VII have been adopted.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act and Notified Body Designation Status

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems under Article 43: internal control (Annex VI) or third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) (low confidence). While the legal framework is reasonably well-documented, the practical infrastructure of designated notified bodies remains underdeveloped, with reports as of early-to-mid 2026 indicating limited or no formal AI Act-specific designations in several sectors (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 provides two pathways for high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system plus technical documentation by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). For biometric systems listed in point 1 of Annex III, providers may choose internal control or notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). Some industry sources interpret Annex VII as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment, though this interpretation carries low confidence ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment), [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation (Section A of Annex I, e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Notified Body Selection and Procedural Rules
Providers may choose any notified body under Annex VII, except where high-risk AI systems are intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from Article 43 procedures temporarily for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Under Annex VII, notified bodies may, as a last resort, request access to training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Administrative Infrastructure
Article 35 establishes rules for identification numbers and public lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)). A Council document references proposed Article 30 codes for AI conformity assessment bodies to be used in the NANDO database (medium confidence), and a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) would create a new Annex XIV listing such codes while amending aviation regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) ([Council document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf), [COM(2025) 836](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but these are separate from AI Act designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Industry sources report that as of March–April 2026, the AI Act notified body ecosystem remains under construction, with no formal AI Act designations yet for medical device AI systems (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). A comparable pattern is reported under the separate Cyber Resilience Act, where zero notified bodies had been designated as of late June 2026 (low confidence) ([CyberCertLabs](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on the applicable deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations: most cite 2 August 2026, while one low-reliability, undated news blog claims a "final text agreed in September 2026" pushed this to 2 August 2029 via an intermediate 2 December 2027 date — this claim is uncorroborated by any official source and should be treated with strong skepticism (low confidence) ([sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026) vs. [unverified blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). Several claims regarding delegated acts under Article 43(5), notified-body certification mechanics, and Article 35 administrative rules rest on single low-authority sources (confidence 0.03–0.17) and should not be treated as settled.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the 2026 Annex III deadline has actually been amended, and if so, by what formal instrument. The precise, verified count of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act (versus MDR/IVDR/CRA) is unavailable. The exact boundary between Annex VI and Annex VII applicability beyond biometrics is not fully specified. The adoption status of COM(2025) 836 and the Article 30 AIP codes is unresolved, as is whether Article 43(5) delegated acts updating Annexes VI/VII have been adopted.
